newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE says signs amended linkage deal with CBOT.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE says signs amended linkage deal with CBOT.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said in a statement on Friday that it had signed an amended linkage agreement with the Chicago Board of Trade.
The amended linkage deal, which removes restrictions on the exchanges' respective electronic trading systems, is scheduled for launch on May 9, 1997, the statement said.
The statement, issued at a derivatives conference in Boca Raton, Florida, was also released in London.

"We remain committed to the historic open outcry linkage between the CBOT and LIFFE which sets the stage for further trading growth in the years ahead," CBOT chairman Patrick H. Arbor said in the statement.
"The partnership moves both exchanges closer to a 24-hour trading day and increases accesibility to both exchanges' premier financial products on both shores," Arbor said.
LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth said the link with the CBOT was of key strategic significance.

"In a period when European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) gives LIFFE its greatest opportunity, our alliance with the CBOT involving our respective premier bond contracts is, obviously, of enormous strategic significance now and in the future," Wigglesworth said in the statement.

LIFFE said that in a related development, Northern Futures Corporation and Tullett & Tokyo were the first clearing members to sign up as linkage partners for clearing and transferring link positions to each other.
"We are both excited about the potential that the CBOT/LIFFE partnership offers to our customers on both shores," said President of Northern Futures David Ganis.
